rules.when: Errand-grade verification and routine chores: reachability or environment checks a human would do by hand, walking a flow in a browser to confirm an entry point, starting or restarting a demo or local stack, preparing demo data, re-running an already-written verification script, and other bounded mechanical work whose steps and success criteria are already known. No root-cause search, no architectural judgement, no gnarly ambiguity.
rules.why: Errand verification and browser chores run on Luna high; Astra is kept for difficult investigation and planning.

rules.when: Moderately difficult engineering work below the difficult-investigation tier: a bounded root-cause diagnosis with a known reproduction path, a non-trivial fix that needs judgement but no cross-cutting redesign, ordinary module or interface design, or a review whose scope and method are already fixed.
rules.why: Sol carries harder bounded engineering and ordinary design without paying for the top tier.

rules.when: Difficult investigations and difficult planning requiring exceptionally high reasoning: unclear or gnarly root-cause investigations, complex cross-cutting architecture redesign, or difficult planning with major unresolved tradeoffs.
rules.why: Astra is the strongest reasoning tier; errands and routine implementation never belong here.

rules.when: Implementation and routine execution with a sufficiently established design: bounded coding changes, tests, routine code-adjacent documentation such as README updates, inline comments and changelog entries, repetitive data collection, and straightforward fixes that do not require architectural decisions or difficult investigation.
rules.why: Routine coding runs on Sol 6.1 medium; reclassify instead of silently widening this tier when the work turns out to need architecture or difficult investigation.
